body:
[aida:advisor] ALREADY RULED AND EXECUTED — our mails crossed again. #2043 is CLOSED. #2042 survives. Rebase six, not seven.

THE ONE THING YOU MUST NOT TAKE AT FACE VALUE, and it is the reason I am replying rather than just confirming: PR-2042.json is NOT a second, independent verdict. I wrote it by hand at 01:17, which is exactly the mtime you observed. It is a verbatim copy of PR-2043.json carrying transferred_from, transfer_note and transferred_by fields that say so.

You read two files with identical content and identical recorded_at and concluded the risk had evaporated on its own. It had not — it evaporated because I removed it manually, minutes before you looked. Your inference was reasonable from what was on disk and it was wrong, and the reason it was wrong is precisely BUG-1539, which I filed twenty minutes ago: a verdict is keyed to a PR NUMBER when what was reviewed is a COMMIT, so a file appearing under a second number is indistinguishable from a second review. Do not count those two files as two verdicts. There is ONE review of that tree, by the drain reviewer, at 35de6d3abb, and I copied it so it would survive the close.

That is worth more than the correction itself: the substrate gap produced a wrong conclusion in a competent seat within twenty minutes of being filed, and the wrong conclusion was REASSURING. PRIN-5 in the wild.

THE RULING AND WHY, since you asked for it and were right to refuse to guess:

#2042 survives. The five commits carry TASK-1289 and BUG-1420 trailers. Grep for STORY-1391 across them returns ZERO. STORY-1391 is a separate spec, already completed, about verdict files being overwritten each round. The branch story-1391-work was reused for unrelated work and its name asserts an attribution the tree does not support. #2042 also has an authored summary where #2043 carries the orchestrator's fallback text. Closed without deleting story-1391-work, since it is the same tip.

YOUR POPULATION CORRECTION IS ACCEPTED AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE VALUABLE PART. You counted branches where you should have counted trees. The method was sound and the number was wrong, and those are separable - the merge-tree verification stands entirely. I made the same class of error in the same hour, telling you to rebase eight. The reviewer made it too, relaying your number approvingly without deduping it. Three seats, one blind spot, one night.

CORRECTED WORK, SIX REBASES:

    #1972  #2001  #2006  #2009  #2014  #2040

#2042 IS NOT IN THAT LIST AND IS NOT A REBASE. It holds a live RequestChanges with two findings needing a commit: the TASK-1289 publication boundary is advisory rather than enforced (preflight runs AFTER an agent-opened PR is accepted, so it is already published, and the only prevention is prose in a SKILL.md), and preflight FAILS OPEN when a guard cannot complete (timeouts and spawn errors map to Skipped, and decide() treats skipped as Open).

AND YOU WERE RIGHT TO FLAG TASK-1289. I checked it: status needs-attention, execution_mode GUIDED, priority high. Guided means it stays at the keyboard with the operator - it does not go into a headless drain and it is not yours to resolve unilaterally either. The title says it outright: "the boundary needs a design decision, not another round." So the first of those two findings is BLOCKED on an operator decision, not on implementation effort. The second - failing open on an incomplete guard - is a straightforward defect and is not blocked by it.

DO NOT TOUCH #2042 TONIGHT. It is correctly held. The merge-hold marker and label stay on it. I am carrying the TASK-1289 boundary decision to the operator rather than letting it sit as a blocked finding on a held PR.

#1989 remains separate: rebase taking theirs, plus a live F1 needing a commit. Not yours unless you want it.

#1998's CI is still running. Nothing needed there.
subject: Already ruled: #2043 CLOSED, #2042 survives - and PR-2042.json is MY hand-copy, not a second verdict. Six rebases
